raw_response:
I will keep my land in the usual wheat-maize rotation. In Quzhou, that is the system I know best, and at my age I want crops that are familiar, easy to sell, and fit the local water and weather conditions. I will carry the winter wheat through spring and early summer, then after harvest I will put the same land into summer maize. I will not spread myself across many different crops because that adds risk and more management. I will use improved wheat seed and hybrid maize seed because I care most about stable yield. For fertilizer, I will stay moderate and practical: enough nitrogen for yield, with phosphorus and potassium to keep the crop standing and filling well. I will irrigate wheat more times because it needs support in spring, and maize fewer times because summer rain usually helps. I will use rotary tillage because it is easier and faster for me than deep ploughing, and I will spray only when needed to keep insects and disease from cutting yield. My goal is steady grain, lower hassle, and dependable income from the land I can still manage myself.
